suite: Unit tests: policy, ledger, reversal, network, interpreter (node --test)
file: tests/credit-math.test.js, tests/engine.test.js, tests/interpreter.test.js, tests/journeys.test.js, tests/network.test.js, tests/reversal.test.js

cases.name: Gupta: ₹78,400 owed + ₹50,000 requested − ₹60,000 limit = ₹68,400 to collect for the full order
Gupta: collecting only ₹38,400 leaves ₹40,000 owed and frees ₹20,000 of the order
Collecting exactly the required amount releases the full order, and never more than owed
Balance already below the limit: part fits today, the rest needs a collection
Order fits fully within the limit: nothing to collect first
No additional credit requested
Requested amount above the limit itself, even with nothing owed: no impossible collection figure
Zero limit: nothing can go on credit
Invalid or negative values are rejected, not computed
1. Gupta Traders, own data only: Watch, ₹75,000, 21-day terms
2. Gupta Traders with eligible network data: ₹60,000, 14-day terms, from the reusable −20% rule
3. Network disabled, or buyer consent revoked: network evidence is excluded and the decision recalculates
4. Chawla Enterprises: Reliable on own data, Watch with network, limit held (uncorroborated rule)
5. New Life Stores, first credit without consent: starter ₹50,000, 15 days, Unrated
6. New Life Stores with valid consent: ₹1,50,000, 21 days; revocation reverts to starter
7. Positive repayment history improves the recommendation within policy limits
8. A failed Autopay updates collection state without marking a default
9. A verified partial payment reduces the invoice outstanding and never adds risk
10. An unverified payment claim does not count as received
11. An existing unmatched payment blocks an inappropriate reminder
12. A Do Not Contact buyer cannot be messaged on WhatsApp (salesperson tasks still allowed)
13. Quiet hours queue the message for the next permitted window (IST)
14. The weekly reminder limit is enforced with the next eligible time
16. A dispute is routed to review and is not classified as default or a missed promise
17. Stale data blocks unsafe execution and lowers confidence
18. Consequential changes are proposals that need merchant approval
20. Portfolio aggregates are internally consistent
Featured scenarios match their expected bands; no buyer is special-cased
Feedback loop: failed Autopay + partial payment + missed promise moves Gupta to Risky, ₹40,000, 7 days
Requests: verdicts come from the same decision
Example 1: "Aadha abhi bhej raha hoon, baaki Monday pakka." → ₹19,200 now, ₹19,200 on Mon 12 Oct (inferred)
Example 2: "Kal 5 hazaar bhejunga, baaki Friday." → ₹5,000 tomorrow, remainder Friday
Example 3: "Monday tak try karunga." → tentative, no invented amount, clarification
Example 4: "Bhai maal short aaya, pehle adjust karo." → dispute, verification suggested
Example 5: "Payment kar diya, UTR bhej raha hoon." → payment claim, unverified, reconcile
Example 6: "Abhi 5000 de sakta hoon, baki agle hafte." → ₹5,000 now, balance date needs clarification
Instructions inside a buyer message are treated as data
Model output checks: fabricated amounts and dates are removed, past dates rejected, sums capped
Request validation
Hinglish examples resolve amounts and IST dates from the demo clock (Mon 5 Oct 2026)
Claims, vague dates, conditions and disputes are never confirmable
Devanagari: claim of ₹5,000 plus a promise of the rest on Monday; evidence stays in the original script
Self-corrections and alternative dates need clarification
Model output: an unstated claimed amount and contradictory dates are caught by validation
The model never sees the buyer name (data minimisation)
J1. The recommendation is ₹60,000 on 14 days, and approving it leaves the recommendation at exactly those values
J2. No compounding: re-evaluating any number of times after approval never shortens terms or lowers the limit
J2b. The old failure mode is gone: current terms of 14 used to step down to 7
J3. Undo: a reversed increase no longer counts toward the 90-day increase cooldown
J5. Failed ₹20,000 collection, then ₹5,000 partial: ₹15,000 remains and the invoice is not settled
J6. Paying the remaining ₹15,000 settles the invoice; the next unpaid invoice is INV-24891
J8. Overpayment and duplicate payments are rejected and leave the ledger unchanged
J8b. A payment claim alone never verifies a payment
J9. Recovery-link minimum: invalid inputs rejected with a reason, valid edits accepted, small balances paid in full
J12. Send safeguards: claim, unmatched review, paid, dispute, DNC, weekly limit, quiet hours, pause, stale, channel and approval
Gupta Traders: own ledger ₹75,000 · 21d; with eligible network ₹60,000 · 14d (corroborated)
Chawla Enterprises: reliable on own data, network disagrees → Watch, limit held (no cut on uncorroborated evidence)
New Life Stores: conservative starter without eligible evidence, raised by rule with it
Consent states: requested and declined/revoked exclude evidence; granted includes it
Insufficient coverage, stale signals and disputes are excluded with a stated reason, and restore cleanly
Participation off: no network evidence for anyone, and the reason says so
Shared logic: the same record under a different id and name gets the same decision (no special-casing)
Valid reversal restores the balance and keeps the original payment in the log
Duplicate reversal is rejected and changes nothing
Unknown payment, non-payment events, wrong amount, wrong invoice and a missing reason are rejected
Partial payment reversal and multiple payments on one invoice: only the reversed one comes back
A reversal can never take an invoice above its amount (stale or conflicting state is rejected)
A reference becomes reusable only after its payment is reversed (correction = reverse + re-record)
A payment split across invoices is one reversal group
Policy ignores reversed payments: a reversed settlement is not on-time evidence
A promise "kept" outcome reopened by a reversal no longer counts as kept
